The June 2018 FOMC statement’s “solid” growth, strong labor market, and inflation near the symmetric 2% objective are broadly corroborated by the Beige Book period (April to mid-May), which reported expansion across Districts and broad-based hiring in retail, business services, technical, manufacturing, and construction. District contacts noted tight labor markets with wage pressures and benefit adjustments, consistent with low unemployment influencing wages. Consumer spending was steady, while credit conditions were not broadly easing: Districts reported mixed loan demand, aligning with SLOOS indications of some tighter policies and uneven demand in CRE and C&I. Net effect: the macro tone remains positive, but Beige Book evidence of capacity constraints and wage pressures, together with mixed credit demand, tempers the exuberance and supports the FOMC’s gradualism and balanced-risk stance.
